new_statements.quote: Le yaouré a quatre (4) tons ponctuels pertinents de base: haut, mi-haut, mi-bas, bas. [...] Les schèmes tonals des bases lexicales sont issus de ces tons ponctuels. (p. 23) — On constate que le yaouré a quatre hauteurs mélodiques pertinentes, c'est-à-dire quatre (4) tonèmes ponctuels: haut (H), mi-haut (MH), mi-bas (MB), et bas (B) [...]. Les tonèmes que nous venons d'identifier sont ponctuels, au sens où seule la hauteur relative constante assume la fonction distinctive. (p. 71)
new_statements.translation: Yaouré has four basic distinctive level tones: high, mid-high, mid-low, low. [...] The tone schemes of lexical bases are built from these level tones. — One observes that Yaouré has four distinctive pitch levels, i.e. four level tonemes: high (H), mid-high (MH), mid-low (MB), and low (B) [...]. The tonemes just identified are level tonemes, in the sense that only constant relative pitch carries the distinctive function.
new_statements.citation: Gadou, Henri. 1992. Quelques aspects des processus phonologiques, morphologiques et énonciatifs de la langue yaouré. Tome I. Thèse de doctorat d'État, Université Paris VII.
new_statements.locator: §1.6.2 'Les niveaux tonals', p. 23 (PDF p. 29); §II.4.2 'Identification des tonèmes du yaouré', p. 71 (PDF p. 77)
new_statements.check: confirmed by a second reader, with minor differences
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (662-page scan, Adobe scanned layer) and extracted PDF p. 29 (= thesis p. 23, §1.6.2 'Les niveaux tonals') and PDF p. 77 (= thesis p. 71, §II.4.1-II.4.3). Both quoted passages are there verbatim; the only differences are scanned artefacts ('ha1ll (H)', 'haut (lI)' for 'haut (H)', 'pennettront' for 'permettront') and the reader's ellipses. p. 23: 'Le yaouré a quatre (4) tons ponctuels pertinents de base: haut, mi-haut, mi-bas, bas.... Les schèmes tonals des bases lexicales sont issus de ces tons ponctuels.' p. 71: 'On constate que le yaouré a quatre hauteurs mélodiques pertinentes, c'est-à-dire quatre (4) tonèmes ponctuels: haut (H), mi-haut (MH), mi-bas (MB), et bas (B)... Les tonème…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Yaouré is a four-level-tone language (H, MH, MB, B, with tone schemes per syllable type and rules of tone spreading, raising, lowering, dissimilation and copying). The source says nothing at all about word stress, accent or prominence; no stress rule can be extracted.
new_statements.exceptions: None relevant; the thesis discusses tone-scheme changes in inflection and compounding, not stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical bases (CV, CVV, CVLV, CVCV) in citation form; tone rules stated across morpheme boundaries. Dialect described: the jàà speech of Canton Yaouré Nord (Bouaflé).
new_statements.identity_note: Gadou 1992 describes the jàà variety of Canton Yaouré Nord (Bouaflé sub-prefecture); Lautenschlager 1992 (not opened) describes the Zégata variety. Both fall under yaou1238 (Glottolog lists no dialect glottocodes). Older names: Kanga-bonou, Yauré, Kwendré 'dialect'. Gadou pp. 13-15 traces the classification history (Tauxier, Westermann & Bryan, Prost, Welmers).
